title: (-1)^(n-1)*a(n) > 0 for all n > 1, and |a(n)|^{1/n} tends to the infinity.
summary: Proved 2026-11-05 (resolutions repo OEIS/A187011; Lean + Mathlib, see README for what is outside Lean). OEIS A187011 (fetched 2026-11-01, edit Aug 2026) still lists the conjecture. Sign part follows from the weighted-tree distance determinant (Bapat-Kirkland-Neumann, LAA 401 (2005), cited from memory): a(n)=(-1)^(n-1)2^(n-2)(p_n-2)prod gaps, checked n<=15. Growth reduces to geometric mean of prime gaps -> infinity, sketched via Brun-type upper bound for prime pairs. See notes/OEIS-A187011.md.
notes: Mathlib proof (A187011_growth_mathlib.lean, assembled by certificate/assemble.py from FAM/twin-primes/twin_primes_mathlib.lean, A187011_mathlib.lean and certificate/Growth.lean.part): A187011_formula: for n >= 2, a n = (-1)^(n-1) 2^(n-2) (p(n-1) - p 0) prod_{i<n-1}(p(i+1) - p i), p = Nat.nth Nat.Prime; A187011_sign: 2 <= n -> 0 < (-1)^(n-1) a n; A187011_growth: Tendsto (fun n => |(a n : R)|^(1/n)) atTop atTop; A187011_conjecture: both. Growth: gaps <= H among the first m give prime pairs q, q+h below p m (smallGap_card_le), bounded by the uniform Selberg bound pairCount_le_log (2^13 K(h)^2 N/log^2 N); Mathlib Chebyshev.pi_ge gives m+1 >= (N log 2 - log(N+1))/log N, so eventually at most m/2 gaps are <= H and log|a n|/n >= (log H)/4.
